title: intent lang init must NOT reinstate the RULES-<lang>/ARCHITECTURE-<lang> fan-out when it is implemented in v3: 10 of 10 were verbatim in Intent and nothing read them
body:
## Summary

`intent lang` is declared in v3 and **unimplemented** (`error: 'lang' is a known command that is not implemented yet`). When it is built, it must not carry over v2's behaviour of installing `intent/llm/RULES-<lang>.md` and `intent/llm/ARCHITECTURE-<lang>.md` per declared language.

This is a **build decision, not a cleanup**. There is nothing to remove in v3 -- the fan-out does not exist there yet. Filed so that implementing the verb does not silently reinstate it by porting `bin/intent_lang:291-312`.

## The evidence, measured 2026-08-24 across five estates

**Intent: 10 of 10 byte-identical to their templates.** Five declared languages, 67 steel threads, self-hosted on v3, in the repo that AUTHORED the templates -- the least favourable case for the conclusion, and it confirmed it. `RULES-<lang>` had **zero** referencing files anywhere in the tree; every hit on `ARCHITECTURE-` was machinery, history, or the files citing themselves.

**The tool had been saying so for months.** `intent_claude_upgrade` emits `REVIEW intent/llm/RULES.md (still verbatim _default template; customise for this project)`. A permanent warning about a decision nobody was going to take -- see issue 0065 for the class.

**Laksa measured the behaviour rather than the file**: `DECISION_TREE.md` instructed-to-read in 51 sessions, actually read in 3. **An instruction to read is not a read.**

## THE CARVE-OUT, AND IT IS THE PART MOST LIKELY TO BE GOT WRONG

**This does NOT apply to the agnostic pair `intent/llm/RULES.md` and `intent/llm/ARCHITECTURE.md`.** Those are a different case with the opposite evidence: **4 of 4 estates measured have AUTHORED theirs** -- Intent (5660B / 9116B, both differing from `_default`), Lamplight, Baize (52 added lines of real architecture), Laksa. Not one left them verbatim.

Same directory, adjacent names, opposite verdict. A sweep that treats `intent/llm/*` as one family deletes the only files in it with real authors.

**And v3 has already dropped them**: `lib/templates/llm/` contains no `_RULES.md` and no `_ARCHITECTURE.md`. That is a regression to repair, tracked separately -- it is invisible today only because the v2 path still seeds them.

## Also: "differs from template" is not "authored"

baize-vc's taxonomy, adopted: a `cmp`-differs file splits **three** ways -- stale-template (older template text, one line, nobody re-seeded), filled, and genuinely authored. Only the last is a stop. A boolean `cmp -s` check reports the first as CUSTOMISED and produces a false stop; read the diff and count ADDED lines, not changed ones.

## Close condition

`intent lang init` ships in v3 installing per-language canon that a project will actually use, and **not** the two markdown files above. If the right answer turns out to be that `lang init` has nothing to install, that is an acceptable close -- the rules it would point at are already served live by `intent claude rules list --lang <lang>`.

## A COUPLING THAT WILL DANGLE, AND IT IS NOT A DEFECT YET

Two shipped skills assert the mechanism by name:

    in-author-essentials/SKILL.md:64   "Per-project canon (`intent/llm/RULES-author.md`,
                                        `intent/llm/ARCHITECTURE-author.md`) lands via
                                        `intent lang init author`."
    in-content-essentials/SKILL.md:65  (the same, for content)

**Those sentences are TRUE today** -- v2's `intent lang init` does install those files, and v2 is what every project on this machine runs. They become FALSE the moment v3's `lang` ships without the fan-out.

So they are deliberately NOT being changed now: editing them today would make canon wrong for the estates that actually run it, in order to be right for a verb that does not exist. **This is the same shape as the `.claude/scripts` line fixed on 2026-08-24** -- a doc describing a mechanism the tool had stopped using -- caught here BEFORE it became false rather than four months after.

Whoever implements `lang` must change these two lines in the same change. That is part of the close condition, not a follow-up.
